review_candidates.title: Senior Program Officer – Virtual Course Development J. Christopher Stevens Digital Leaders Program
review_candidates.description: FLSA STATUS : Exempt Pay: $65,000-$75,000 POSITION SUMMARY The Senior Program Officer – Virtual Course Development will help lead the design, coordination, and implementation of curriculum and online learning components for the J. Christopher Stevens Digital Leaders Program, a U.S. Department of State-funded program that connects participants in the United States and the Middle East and North Africa. The program includes four interconnected components that build on one another: short-term virtual exchanges focused on leadership and professional skills development; virtual internships and project-based learning opportunities with U.S. and MENA organizations; in-person Alumni Accelerator workshops centered on themes such as STEM, artificial intelligence, digital media, entrepreneurship, and peacebuilding; and alumni seed funding to support participant-led community impact projects. The Senior Program Officer will support instructional quality and ensure that program content aligns with project goals related to leadership development, cross-cultural exchange, digital engagement, and workforce readiness. Working closely with the Program Manager and broader program team, the Senior Program Officer will coordinate with facilitators, staff, and partner organizations to develop engaging and accessible virtual learning experiences for participant audiences. The position requires strong project management skills, experience in curriculum or online learning development, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced international program environment. This role will report to the Program Manager. This is a Washington, D.C.-based position with a hybrid schedule of office and work-from home days (minimum two in-office days). POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES Assists the Senior Program Manager in the development, coordination, and implementation of virtual exchange course content and learning materials; Coordinates with facilitators, subject matter experts, instructional designers, and partner organizations to ensure high-quality curriculum delivery; Oversees course timelines, deliverables, and production schedules to support successful implementation across multiple program activities; Supports participant application review, orientation, and on-program assistance; Supports the integration of leadership development, intercultural learning, digital communication, and workforce readiness content into program curricula; Reviews course materials and activities to ensure alignment with program objectives, accessibility standards, and donor requirements; Supports facilitator onboarding, training, and ongoing coordination related to curriculum implementation; Monitors participant feedback and evaluation data to identify opportunities for curriculum improvement and innovation; Tracks attendance, participant, and completion records; Collaborates with communications and alumni staff to support participant engagement and dissemination of program resources; Supports Canvas integration, participant and facilitator technology training, and participant request for technology access assistance; Coordinates alumni mentoring program; Drafts reports, briefing materials, work plans, and curriculum-related documentation; Provides updates to the Program Manager and Senior Program Manager on course development progress, challenges, and recommendations; and Other duties as assigned. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree, preferably in education, instructional design, international education, international relations, communications, or a related field; Minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in curriculum development, online learning, international education, youth programming, or virtual exchange initiatives; Experience developing or managing online, hybrid, or virtual learning programs; Professional experience with back-end management of learning management platforms, Zoom and Canvas strongly preferred; Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage complex workflows; Demonstrated success facilitating virtual meetings/activities; Excellent writing, editing, and verbal communication skills; Ability to effectively juggle multiple tasks and deadlines at the same time; High level of interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity to interact effectively with participants, partners, consultants, and staff across backgrounds; Experience coordinating with cross-functional teams and external stakeholders; Capacity to work both independently and as a member of a team; and Ability to take initiative, solve problems, and adapt in a fast-paced environment.   PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Master’s degree in education, instructional design, international education, or a related field; Experience supporting U.S. government-funded or donor-funded international programs; Experience with virtual exchange, intercultural dialogue, or global engagement programming; Professional experience with Microsoft Office Suite; Experience developing facilitation guides, training resources, or participant learning materials; and Ability and willingness to travel if needed. review_candidates.title: Senior Civil Inspector
review_candidates.description: Overview The Senior Civil Inspector is responsible for inspecting, monitoring and verifying civil construction activities for the Hydroelectric Power Plant to ensure that all works executed by the EPCC Contractor and its Subcontractors comply with the approved AFC Drawings, Project Specifications, Method Statements, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), applicable codes and standards, and contractual requirements. The position will provide day-to-day site inspection and technical support for civil construction works, monitor construction quality and progress, identify non-conformances, verify completed works and maintain proper inspection and site records. The Senior Civil Inspector shall report to the Project Manager and work closely with the Project Engineering, QA/QC, HSSE, Planning and EPCC Contractor teams. Job Responsibilities Civil Construction Inspection Conduct daily inspection and surveillance of civil construction activities to ensure compliance with approved AFC Drawings, specifications, method statements and ITPs. Inspect hydroelectric power plant civil works including: Dam and associated structures; Intake, spillway and outlet structures; Headrace, tailrace, tunnels and underground works; Powerhouse and associated buildings; Penstock and support structures; Foundations and reinforced/mass concrete structures; Access roads, drainage and retaining structures; Slope stabilisation and other associated infrastructure. Verify construction dimensions, alignment, levels, elevations and workmanship against approved drawings. Identify defective, incomplete or non-compliant works and ensure appropriate rectification. Verify completed rectification works prior to acceptance. Concrete, Earthworks and Foundation Works Inspect reinforcement, formwork, embedded items, construction joints, waterstops and concrete placement. Witness pre-pour inspections and concrete quality testing. Monitor concrete batching, placement, vibration, curing and finishing. Inspect excavation, rock excavation, foundation preparation, backfilling and compaction works. Monitor rock support, rock bolts, shotcrete, anchors, drainage and slope protection works. Witness and verify relevant field testing, laboratory testing and material testing. Tunnel and Underground Works Monitor tunnel excavation and underground construction activities. Inspect tunnel profiles, rock support, rock bolts, shotcrete, steel supports, waterproofing, drainage and concrete lining. Verify construction works against approved tunnel support systems and methodology. Report unexpected geological conditions or construction issues to the Construction Engineer. Quality Assurance / Quality Control Review and understand relevant Project Specifications, AFC Drawings, ITPs, Method Statements and Quality Plans. Witness Hold Points, Witness Points and required inspection activities. Monitor the EPCC Contractor's compliance with approved quality procedures. Review inspection records, material certificates and test results. Raise and monitor Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and ensure corrective actions are properly implemented. Monitor and close civil construction punch-list items. Progress Monitoring and Reporting Monitor daily construction progress against the approved project schedule. Maintain daily inspection reports, site diaries, photographs and records. Record manpower, equipment, construction activities, site constraints and major issues. Highlight construction delays, quality issues and technical concerns to the Construction Engineer. Verify actual physical progress and completed quantities for progress measurement and payment assessment. Contractor Management Monitor the performance of the EPCC Contractor and Subcontractors in relation to construction quality and compliance. Ensure construction activities are carried out in accordance with approved drawings, procedures and method statements. Coordinate with contractor engineers, supervisors, surveyors and QA/QC personnel to resolve site issues. Monitor and follow up outstanding construction works, defects and NCRs until closure. HSSE and Environmental Compliance Monitor civil construction activities for compliance with approved HSSE and environmental requirements. Report unsafe acts, unsafe conditions and environmental non-compliance. Ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with approved permits and safe work procedures. Monitor relevant environmental controls, including erosion, sediment control, watercourse protection, spoil disposal and construction waste management. Completion and Handover Support inspection and verification of completed civil works. Participate in final inspection, testing and commissioning activities where applicable. Verify completion and closure of civil punch-list items. Review and verify as-built drawings, inspection records, test results and other handover documentation. Support the Project Team during project completion, taking-over and defect rectification activities. Key Deliverables The Senior Civil Inspector shall maintain and/or contribute to: Daily Site Inspection Reports and site records. Work Inspection Requests (WIR/IR). Inspection and Test Plan records. Concrete inspection and testing records. Material inspection and test certificates. Survey and dimensional verification records. NCR and corrective action records. Civil punch-list and outstanding works register. Construction progress and photographic records. As-built verification records. Civil completion and handover documentation. Qualifications and Experience Education Diploma or Degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering or related discipline . Relevant professional certification or registration will be an advantage. Experience Minimum 8 years of relevant civil construction experience , preferably in major infrastructure, hydropower, dam, tunnel or power plant projects. Proven experience in hydroelectric power plant civil works is highly preferred. Experience in site inspection, construction supervision, QA/QC and EPCC Contractor management. Experience in concrete structures, earthworks, rock excavation, foundations, tunnelling and hydraulic structures. Familiarity with AFC Drawings, Project Specifications, ITPs, Method Statements, NCRs and construction quality requirements. Technical Competencies Hydropower and hydraulic structures. Reinforced and mass concrete works. Earthworks and excavation. Rock excavation and foundation treatment. Tunnel and underground works. Grouting and slope stabilisation. Survey and dimensional control. Construction QA/QC and inspection. Contractor and Subcontractor coordination. Construction progress monitoring. Applicable codes, standards and statutory requirements. Job Summary The QA/QC Officer will be responsible for monitoring and maintaining quality standards across the company’s construction projects and operational activities. The role involves developing and implementing quality control procedures, inspecting construction materials and completed works, coordinating material testing, identifying non-conformities and ensuring that corrective actions are implemented promptly. The ideal candidate must demonstrate strong technical knowledge of construction processes, materials and quality assurance practices, excellent analytical skills, attention to detail and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced construction environment. Key Responsibilities   1. Quality Assurance Planning and Implementation ·      Develop, implement and maintain project-specific quality assurance and quality control procedures in line with approved project specifications, drawings, contractual requirements and applicable standards. ·      Prepare and implement project quality plans, inspection and test plans (ITPs), quality checklists and other relevant quality documentation. ·      Establish quality control checkpoints for construction activities to ensure compliance at every stage of project execution. ·      Review construction drawings, technical specifications, method statements and material requirements to identify quality-related concerns before work commences. 2. Construction Site Inspection and Quality Control ·      Conduct routine inspections of construction activities, materials, workmanship and completed works to verify compliance with approved specifications and quality standards. ·    Inspect key construction activities, including concrete works, reinforcement installation, formwork, masonry, structural works, finishing and other relevant activities, according to project scope. ·   Verify that construction works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, technical specifications, applicable codes and established industry practices. ·      Inspect completed work before it progresses to subsequent construction stages or is presented for client or consultant approval. ·      Identify defects, deviations, substandard workmanship and other quality issues, and ensure they are documented and addressed. 3. Materials Inspection and Testing ·  Inspect construction materials delivered to project sites to verify compliance with approved specifications, quality requirements and relevant standards. ·     Verify material certificates, test reports, manufacturer documentation and other quality records before materials are approved for use. ·     Coordinate the sampling and testing of construction materials, including cement, aggregates, concrete, reinforcement steel, blocks, soil and other materials relevant to project activities. ·      Liaise with approved laboratories, suppliers, consultants and site personnel to ensure required tests are conducted and results are properly documented. ·     Ensure that materials failing to meet specified requirements are identified, segregated where applicable and prevented from unauthorised use. 4. Non-Conformance Management and Corrective Actions ·     Identify, document and report non-conformities relating to materials, workmanship, construction processes and project deliverables. ·      Issue or coordinate the issuance of non-conformance reports (NCRs) in accordance with approved company procedures. ·     Investigate recurring quality issues and support root-cause analysis to determine the reasons for defects and deviations. ·      Recommend corrective and preventive actions and follow up to ensure they are implemented within agreed timelines. 5. Quality Documentation and Reporting ·   Maintain accurate and up-to-date quality records, including inspection reports, material test results, checklists, NCRs, corrective action logs and quality approvals. ·  Prepare periodic QA/QC reports highlighting inspection outcomes, quality concerns, outstanding corrective actions and overall project quality performance. ·    Maintain a traceable record of materials, tests, inspections and approvals throughout the construction process. ·     Ensure that quality documentation is properly organised and readily available for internal reviews, client inspections, consultant assessments and external audits. 6. Quality Audits and Compliance Monitoring ·     Conduct internal quality audits and routine compliance checks to assess adherence to approved quality management procedures. ·   Monitor compliance with applicable Nigerian construction requirements, relevant building codes, recognised engineering standards and contractual quality obligations. ·   Identify gaps in quality processes and recommend practical improvements to strengthen project delivery. ·      Support client, consultant and third-party quality inspections and audits. ·      Follow up on audit findings and ensure that corrective actions are implemented and documented. ·      Monitor changes to approved drawings, specifications and work procedures to ensure that quality controls reflect the latest authorised requirements. 7. Project Coordination and Stakeholder Management ·      Work closely with project managers, site engineers, quantity surveyors, procurement personnel, subcontractors, suppliers and consultants to maintain consistent quality standards. ·     Participate in project meetings to discuss quality performance, outstanding defects, inspection schedules and corrective actions. ·     Coordinate inspection requests and testing schedules in line with project work programmes to minimise avoidable delays. ·      Liaise with clients and consultants during inspections and obtain the required quality approvals at designated project stages. 8. Quality Improvement and Risk Prevention ·     Identify opportunities to improve construction processes, material utilisation and overall project quality. ·     Analyse quality performance data to identify recurring defects, process weaknesses and areas requiring additional controls. ·     Recommend preventive measures to reduce rework, avoid material wastage and improve compliance with approved specifications. ·     Participate in lessons-learned reviews and incorporate relevant findings into future quality plans and procedures. Qualifications and Experience ·    Bachelor’s degree or HND in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Building Technology, Construction Management or a related discipline. ·   Minimum of 3–5 years of relevant QA/QC experience, preferably within the construction, civil engineering, infrastructure or building industry. ·     Professional certification or training in quality management, quality assurance or quality control is an added advantage. ·   Demonstrable experience conducting construction site inspections, materials testing coordination, quality audits and non-conformance management. ·     Good understanding of construction drawings, technical specifications, material standards, construction methods and quality inspection procedures. ·     Familiarity with relevant Nigerian building regulations, applicable engineering standards and recognised quality management principles, including ISO 9001 where applicable. ·      Experience preparing inspection and test plans, quality reports, non-conformance reports and other technical documentation. ·      Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and other relevant reporting or project management tools. ·      Ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications and identify deviations from approved requirements. ·      Willingness to travel to construction sites and other project locations as required. Required Skills and Competencies The ideal candidate must demonstrate: ·      Strong technical knowledge of construction materials, processes and quality control methods. ·      Excellent analytical, inspection and problem-solving skills. ·      High levels of integrity, accuracy, accountability and attention to detail. ·      Ability to identify defects, investigate quality issues and recommend effective corrective actions. ·      Strong documentation, report-writing and record-keeping skills. ·      Effective communication and collaboration with technical teams, subcontractors, suppliers and management. ·      Ability to enforce quality standards professionally, even under pressure to meet project deadlines. ·      Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple inspections and competing priorities. ·     A proactive approach to defect prevention, continuous improvement and quality risk management. ·     Ability to work independently, exercise sound technical judgement and escalate critical quality concerns appropriately. What We Offer ·       An opportunity to contribute to significant construction and infrastructure projects. ·       A performance-driven and professionally challenging work environment. ·       Opportunities for career development and professional growth. ·   The opportunity to contribute to strengthening quality management systems and improving construction delivery standards across the organisation. ·      Competitive remuneration commensurate with qualifications and experience.
